title: Engineering identity
intro: Not a résumé. Five layers I grew through: what I built in each, what it gave the team, and what it changed in me.

layers.name: Network
layers.whatChanged: I learned how machines actually talk to each other, before I ever wrote the software on top.
built: Researched static-routing scenarios so the QC team could test the company's own routers and switches.
Ran functional and quality tests on networking products before release.
Wrote documentation on Cisco and networking technologies for the team.
forTheTeam: Test scenarios the QC team could reuse on every new router and switch build.
Written knowledge instead of knowledge in one person's head.
forMe: Packets, routes and failure modes: the layer every system I build later runs on.
Repeating the same test by hand made me want to automate it. That pulled me into code.

layers.name: Backend
layers.whatChanged: I stopped running tests and started building the system that runs them.
built: Custom Python packages that automated the QC team's daily work.
The backend of a web platform for running automated tests, with Django and Django REST Framework.
Scheduled and async jobs with Celery and RabbitMQ.
forTheTeam: Tests started from a web app instead of from someone's terminal.
Repetitive QC work turned into reusable packages.
forMe: How to design APIs, data models and background jobs that other people depend on.
Clean code and documentation matter more once a team uses what you wrote.

layers.name: DevOps
layers.role: Developer who ships his own systems
layers.whatChanged: I learned DevOps as a developer: if I build it, I should be able to ship it, run it and fix it.
built: CI/CD pipelines in GitLab and Jenkins for Dev, Staging and Prod.
Parallel Jenkins pipelines so network tests run concurrently instead of one after another.
Test artifacts stored in MinIO, collected by Celery jobs and written to a database.
A private Nexus registry for versioned container images.
Python and Bash automation for managing test devices.
forTheTeam: The QC test platform (ZAts) went from manual runs to automated, parallel pipelines: shorter test cycles and more accurate results.
More stable, repeatable releases across Dev, Staging and Prod.
forMe: Containers, pipelines and Linux servers stopped being someone else's job.
Shipping my own apps end to end. Once they were live, I wanted to know what the data inside them was saying.

layers.name: Data
layers.whatChanged: I stopped seeing data as tables and started seeing it as a system.
built: Designed and implemented the company's Modern Data Stack from scratch.
Moved reporting from ETL to ELT: land raw data first, model it in the warehouse with dbt.
Change data capture from production databases with Debezium and Kafka Connect.
Real-time processing with Flink and a real-time warehouse on Apache Doris.
A historical lake on Apache Iceberg (Parquet) that Doris queries directly.
forTheTeam: One platform for data that used to live in SQL databases, MongoDB, Elastic, spreadsheets, PDFs and external APIs.
Fresher numbers: changes stream from production instead of waiting for batch exports.
Tested dbt models, lineage and row-level masking, so reports can be trusted and shared safely.
BI, data science and internal services all read from the same source of truth.
forMe: Data pipelines, data reliability and analytics systems.
Thinking in streams, contracts and lineage, not just queries.

layers.name: AI
layers.whatChanged: Now I'm learning to put intelligence on top of the data system.
built: AI analysis of customer support tickets with LangChain, traced and evaluated with Langfuse.

ghost.text: There is always another P0. Follow it in /lab.
